title: Resignation, removal and replacement of auditors
subject: This guide addresses the resignation, removal, and replacement of auditors for public companies, registered schemes, registrable superannuation entities, AFS licensees, and credit licensees. It explains ASIC's power to consent to or approve changes of auditor under the Corporations Act and National Credit Regulations.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009 (Cth) and related regulations. It is intended for public companies, corporate directors of retail corporate collective investment vehicles, responsible entities, trustees, AFS licensees, credit licensees, and their auditors, providing clarity on the process for changing auditors.
ruling: ASIC will consider applications for consent or approval to change an auditor based on whether there are reasonable grounds for the proposed change. ASIC expects the applicant to demonstrate that the change is not due to any disagreement over accounting or auditing issues that would warrant further investigation. In assessing applications, ASIC may seek further information or refer matters to the relevant professional body. The guide outlines that ASIC will generally grant consent if no concerns arise, but may refuse or require additional steps if there are unresolved issues with the existing auditor. ASIC also emphasizes the role of directors and audit committees in considering the reasons for a change and ensuring proper professional standards are maintained.
